mainTopic: Wall distances (לבוד vs. four אמות), imagined walls (גוד אסיק, דיומד) in רבי יעקב's four-posts case, and the source for a סוכה's ten-טפחים minimum height
overview: This amud covers three topics. First, it finishes a case about a סוכה that is too short, where the floor was dug out to make it ten טפחים tall. The dug-out area must be less than three טפחים from the wall, because the short wall only becomes a wall through לבוד. In contrast, an existing wall can count for a platform up to four אמות away. Next, אביי suggests that a ten-טפח pillar inside a סוכה taller than twenty אמה works through גוד אסיק מחיצתא, but רבא rejects this because a סוכה needs walls that can be seen. Then the גמרא discusses four posts with סכך on top, where רבי יעקב says kosher and the חכמים say not kosher. רב הונא places their argument on the edge of the roof and רב נחמן places it in the middle. רב הונא is refuted about the middle of the roof, and a ברייתא explains that for רבי יעקב thick posts count as corner pieces (דיומד). Finally, the גמרא asks where the ten-טפחים minimum height comes from and begins its answer with the ארון and the כפורת, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Less than three handbreadths from the wall makes it kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its ruling on the dug-out סוכה: if the dug-out area is less than three טפחים from the wall, the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the gap is less than three handbreadths, the סוכה is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began just before this line. A סוכה too short to count was made taller by digging out the floor, and if the dug-out part is less than three טפחים from the wall, the סוכה is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall alone is shorter than ten טפחים, so it is not a real wall. When the gap between the dug-out edge and the wall is under three טפחים, the two are treated as joined (לבוד), and together they reach ten טפחים. With a gap of three טפחים or more, they are not joined, so there is no proper wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three handbreadths, the classic size limit for treating a gap as closed
Kosher, valid for use
The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if it were closed
A handbreadth, a basic unit of measure

steps.confusionAlert: This line finishes a case from the previous lines: a short סוכה whose floor was dug out to make it ten טפחים tall. The 'three טפחים' is the distance between the dug-out area and the wall, not the height of anything.

phrases.english: Less than three handbreadths — it is kosher.
phrases.notes: This is the distance from the edge of the dug-out area to the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling about the dug-out סוכה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dug-out area less than three טפחים from the wall joins the wall through לבוד, and the סוכה is kosher.

steps.title: Why four cubits there but only three handbreadths here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: the platform case allowed a gap of up to four אמות, but the dug-out case allows less than three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? There you said less than four cubits, and here you said less than three handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares two rulings that look inconsistent. In the earlier case, a platform built inside a very tall סוכה could be up to four אמות from the wall. Here, the dug-out area must be less than three טפחים from the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases ask how far a wall can be from the usable area and still count. Four אמות is far more than three טפחים, so the גמרא wants to know why the allowed gap is so different. It is asking for the logic that separates the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A formula that asks why two similar cases get different rulings
There / here, pointing to the earlier case and the current case
Four cubits, the distance allowed in the platform case
That you said, referring back to an earlier ruling

phrases.english: What is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the earlier case: a סוכה over twenty אמה tall with a raised platform built inside it.

phrases.english: that you said less than four cubits,
and what is different here,
that you said less than three handbreadths?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּאָמְרַתְּ פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-טפחים limit from step 1 by comparing it with the four-אמות limit in the earlier platform case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different distance limits in the platform case (four אמות) and the dug-out case (three טפחים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two cases that both ask how far a wall may be from the usable area get very different measurements, which looks inconsistent.

steps.title: A real wall versus a wall that still needs to be created
steps.stepSummary: In the platform case a real wall already exists, so four אמות is enough. In the dug-out case the wall must be made into a wall through לבוד, which only works under three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, where a wall already exists, less than four cubits is enough. Here, to turn it into a wall, less than three handbreadths works, and otherwise it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. In one case the wall already exists. In the other, the wall must still be created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the tall סוכה, the walls are full, proper walls; the only question is whether they count for the platform, and a gap under four אמות is acceptable. In the short סוכה, the wall is under ten טפחים, so it is not a wall at all until it joins the dug-out area. That joining depends on לבוד, which only works for gaps under three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: It exists, it is already there
A wall of the סוכה
It is enough, it is sufficient
To make it into, to give it the status of
Yes / no

steps.whatToRemember: Four אמות works when a real wall already exists and only needs to count for the usable area. Three טפחים (לבוד) is needed when the gap-closing is what creates the wall in the first place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key distinction: giving an existing wall to an area is easier than creating a wall that is not there yet.

phrases.english: There, where the wall exists,
phrases.notes: In the tall סוכה, the walls are already full, proper walls.

phrases.english: less than four cubits is enough;
here, to make it into a wall,
phrases.notes: The short wall does not count as a wall until it joins up with the dug-out area.

phrases.english: less than three handbreadths, yes;
if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are the same kind of wall question, so they should use the same distance.
steps.terutzMaskana: An existing wall can count for an area up to four אמות away, but creating a wall depends on לבוד, which works only under three טפחים.

steps.title: A ten-handbreadth pillar inside a too-tall סוכה: אביי's first thought
steps.stepSummary: New case: a סוכה over twenty אמה tall has a pillar ten טפחים high with enough surface for a סוכה. אביי first thinks it is kosher because of גוד אסיק מחיצתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was taller than twenty cubits, and he built a pillar in it ten handbreadths high with the minimum size of a סוכה on top, אביי thought to say: extend the walls upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case about a pillar inside a סוכה that is too tall. It presents אביי's first idea that the pillar could work, and it is setting up a discussion that will test that idea next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pillar is ten טפחים high, so its sides count as walls. With גוד אסיק מחיצתא, we picture those sides extending upward to the סכך, which creates a small, kosher-height סוכה on top of the pillar. The phrase 'סבר אביי למימר' signals only a first thought, which the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: A pillar or column
The minimum size of a kosher סוכה, seven by seven טפחים
Extend and raise the walls: we treat a wall as if it continues upward
He thought to say: a first idea that may later be changed

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר אביי למימר' does not give the final halacha. It is only אביי's starting idea, which the גמרא is about to test.

phrases.english: If it was higher than twenty cubits,
and he built in it a pillar
phrases.notes: The pillar stands away from the walls, out in the middle of the סוכה.

phrases.english: that is ten handbreadths high,
and it has the minimum size of a sukkah
phrases.notes: The top of the pillar is at least seven by seven טפחים.

phrases.english: Abaye thought to say,
"Extend and raise the walls."
phrases.notes: The sides of the pillar are pictured as reaching upward, forming walls around the space above it.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר אַבָּיֵי לְמֵימַר גּוּד אַסֵּיק מְחִיצָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case in the series of ways to fix a סוכה that is too tall or too short.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's first view: a ten-טפחים pillar with seven by seven טפחים on top inside a too-tall סוכה is kosher, because its sides are extended upward (גוד אסיק מחיצתא).

steps.title: רבא rejects אביי: walls must be visible
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells אביי that the pillar cannot count as a kosher סוכה, because a סוכה needs walls that can be seen, and the pillar has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We need walls that can be seen, and here there aren't any.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against אביי's idea from the last step. He says that imagining the pillar's sides stretching upward is not enough, because a סוכה needs walls you can actually see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי wanted to use גוד אסיק מחיצתא: picture the edges of the pillar extending upward to make walls. רבא answers that this only works when there is a noticeable wall to extend. On top of the pillar nothing sticks up at all, so there is no visible wall, and the סוכה is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Walls that are noticeable, meaning you can actually see them
We need / we require
There isn't any / it is missing

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, an imagined wall extension (גוד אסיק) needs a real, visible wall to start from. The bare top of a pillar does not count.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting גוד אסיק מחיצתא as a whole. He is only saying it does not work here, because nothing visible is there to extend.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is אביי, who said in the last step that the pillar works.

phrases.english: We require partitions that are noticeable,
and there are none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: בָּעֵינַן מְחִיצוֹת הַנִּיכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's ruling in step 4 that the pillar סוכה is kosher.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using גוד אסיק מחיצתא for the pillar case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pillar has no visible walls at all, and a סוכה needs walls that can be seen.

steps.title: Four posts with roofing: רבי יעקב vs. the Sages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone stuck in four posts and put סכך on top of them. רבי יעקב says the סוכה is kosher and the חכמים say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone stuck in four posts and put roofing on top of them, רבי יעקב says it is kosher and the חכמים say it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a סוכה built from four posts with סכך on top and no regular walls. This sets up the next steps, which ask where exactly this dispute applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case connects to the same topic of imagined walls. Here there are only four posts holding up the סכך. רבי יעקב says that is enough and the חכמים say it is not, and the ברייתא does not say why.

keyTerms.meaning: Posts or poles
He stuck into the ground / planted
He put down the סכך (the roofing)
Rules it kosher
Rule it not kosher

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one stuck in four posts
and placed roofing on top of them,
Rabbi Yaakov rules it kosher
and the Sages rule it not kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the related subject of walls that are not really there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four posts with סכך on top: רבי יעקב says kosher, the חכמים say not kosher.

steps.title: רב הונא: the dispute is on the edge of the roof
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the dispute is about posts standing right on the edge of a roof, above the walls of the house. רבי יעקב uses גוד אסיק מחיצתא and the חכמים do not. In the middle of the roof, everyone agrees the סוכה is not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The argument is when the posts are on the edge of the roof. רבי יעקב holds that we say 'extend the walls upward,' and the Sages hold that we don't say 'extend the walls upward.' But in the middle of the roof, everyone agrees it is not kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains where the ברייתא's argument happens. He places it on the edge of a roof, where the house walls are right below the posts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the edge of the roof, the house's own walls are directly under the posts. רבי יעקב imagines those walls continuing upward to surround the סוכה (גוד אסיק). The חכמים do not accept that idea. In the middle of the roof there are no walls underneath to extend, so even רבי יעקב agrees it is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge of the roof
Picture the wall as extending up: an existing wall counts as if it rises higher
The middle of the roof
Everyone agrees

steps.whyThisMatters: According to רב הונא, the whole argument comes down to one question: do we accept גוד אסיק מחיצתא?

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The dispute is on the edge of the roof,
for Rabbi Yaakov holds:
we say, "Extend and raise the partition,"
and the Rabbis hold:
we do not say, "Extend and raise the partition."
But in the middle of the roof,
everyone agrees it is not kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַחְלוֹקֶת עַל שְׂפַת הַגָּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where and why the ברייתא's argument in step 6 applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Edge of roof: argument over גוד אסיק. Middle of roof: not kosher according to everyone.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the dispute is in the middle of the roof
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב הונא and says the ברייתא's argument is about posts in the middle of the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: The argument is in the middle of the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different explanation from רב הונא. He says רבי יעקב and the חכמים argue even in the middle of the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said that in the middle of the roof everyone agrees it is not kosher. רב נחמן says that is the very case they argue about. In the middle of the roof there are no house walls below to extend, so for רבי יעקב the posts themselves must be enough. Steps 16-17 show how: each post can count as an L-shaped corner piece (דיומד).

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute / an argument

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
In the middle of the roof there is a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בְּאֶמְצַע הַגָּג מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא about which case the ברייתא is discussing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יעקב and the חכמים argue even about posts in the middle of the roof.

steps.title: What does רב נחמן hold about the edge of the roof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רב נחמן's view: does everyone agree the edge of the roof is kosher, or do they argue there too?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the argument only in the middle of the roof, while on the edge of the roof everyone agrees it is kosher? Or maybe they argue in both cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about רב נחמן. He told us they argue in the middle of the roof, but he did not say what happens on the edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read רב נחמן. Maybe on the edge of the roof everyone agrees it is kosher, because the house walls below help. Or maybe the חכמים still say it is not kosher even on the edge, so they argue in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (a real question the גמרא wants answered)
Or maybe
Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is there a dispute in the middle of the roof,
phrases.notes: This is asking what רב נחמן meant.

phrases.english: but on the edge of the roof
everyone agrees it is kosher,
or perhaps
there is a dispute both in this case and in that case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רב נחמן's statement means for the edge of the roof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רב נחמן, is the edge-of-the-roof case kosher according to everyone, or is it also argued about?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds no answer, so the question is left open with the word תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (the question stays unanswered).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא could not settle the question about רב נחמן, so it closes the discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question was asked properly but no proof was found either way. So we do not know whether רב נחמן thinks the edge-of-the-roof case is argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the argument is on the edge of the roof (over גוד אסיק), and the middle is not kosher for everyone. רב נחמן: they argue in the middle of the roof. What he holds about the edge is left as תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean either side is wrong. It only means the גמרא did not find an answer.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question from step 9 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether רב נחמן holds that they argue about the edge of the roof stays unresolved.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא about posts stuck in the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the posts were stuck בָּאָרֶץ, in the ground, and still רבי יעקב rules the סוכה kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If someone stuck four posts into the ground and put סכך on top of them, רבי יעקב says it is kosher and the חכמים say it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא to set up an attack on רב הונא. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument between רבי יעקב and the חכמים we saw before. This version adds one important word: בָּאָרֶץ, 'in the ground.' That word is what the גמרא will use against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: In the ground: the one new word in this version of the ברייתא, which the גמרא builds its question on

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If one stuck four posts into the ground
and put סכך on top of them,
רבי יעקב rules it kosher, and the חכמים rule it not kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question about רב נחמן ends in תיקו, the גמרא goes back to challenge רב הונא from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that everyone agrees the middle of the roof is not kosher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it brings a version of the ברייתא that places the posts in the ground.

steps.title: Ground is like the middle of the roof, yet רבי יעקב allows it
steps.stepSummary: Ground has no walls under it, just like the middle of a roof. Since רבי יעקב rules it kosher, it seems he allows the middle of a roof too, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ground is just like the middle of the roof, and still רבי יעקב rules it kosher! This is a refutation of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא. It says the ground case is really a 'middle of the roof' case, and רבי יעקב still says kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא explained רבי יעקב's view with גוד אסיק מחיצתא: the house walls below the roof's edge stretch up. Posts in the ground have no walls below them at all, just like the middle of a roof. So רבי יעקב must allow even the middle of a roof. That contradicts רב הונא's claim that everyone agrees it is not kosher there.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle of the roof, where there are no house walls directly below
Is similar to, is treated like
'Stretch the wall up': walls below are treated as if they rise higher

phrases.english: But the ground is like the middle of the roof,
phrases.notes: In both cases there are no walls underneath the posts that could be stretched upward.

phrases.english: and yet רבי יעקב rules it kosher!
This is a refutation of רב הונא,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the word בָּאָרֶץ from the ברייתא in step 11 to attack רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that in the middle of the roof everyone agrees the סוכה is not kosher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ground equals middle of the roof (no walls below). רבי יעקב rules ground kosher, so there is an argument even in the middle of the roof.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: this is a real refutation of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the first attack. It agrees that רב הונא's view has been disproved on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רב הונא here. So his claim that everyone agrees the middle of the roof is not kosher is rejected. The ברייתא shows רבי יעקב allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a source that disproves a view. Said twice, it means the view is truly rejected.

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא loses on the 'middle of the roof': רבי יעקב rules even that case kosher.

phrases.english: It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the attack in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is refuted: רבי יעקב and the חכמים argue even about posts in the middle of the roof.

steps.title: A possible second refutation about the edge of the roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא also implies that at the edge of the roof everyone agrees the סוכה is kosher. That would refute רב הונא a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: it is in the middle that they argue, but on the edge of the roof everyone agrees it is kosher! Shall we say רב הונא is refuted on two counts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second attack on רב הונא from the same ברייתא, this time about the edge of the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא puts the argument in the middle-like case, maybe that means the edge is not argued about. Then everyone would agree the edge is kosher. But רב הונא said the edge is exactly where they argue, so he would be wrong twice.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adding another point
The edge of the roof, right above the house walls
Everyone agrees
On two counts

phrases.english: And furthermore:
it is in the middle that they argue,
but on the edge of the roof
everyone agrees it is kosher!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא doesn't say this outright. The גמרא is reading it from the fact that the argument was set in the middle.

phrases.english: Shall we say there is a refutation
of רב הונא on two counts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second attack on רב הונא from the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the argument is about the edge of the roof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument is placed in the middle, which implies that at the edge everyone agrees it is kosher.

steps.title: רב הונא: the argument covers the edge too
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא can answer that they argue at the edge as well. The ברייתא picked the middle only to show how far רבי יעקב goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: they argue about the middle of the roof, and the same is true about the edge of the roof. The reason they argue about the middle is to show you the strength of רבי יעקב's view, that he rules it kosher even in the middle of the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא against the second attack only. It explains why the ברייתא chose the middle case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle case is the harder one for רבי יעקב. A ברייתא picks the extreme case to show how far his view reaches, not to say the easier edge case is agreed upon. So the חכמים can still disagree at the edge, and רב הונא is refuted only once, not twice.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same law applies
To show you the strength (how far) of someone's view
Even ... also

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא is refuted about the middle of the roof. He is not refuted about the edge, because the ברייתא may have picked the middle just to show רבי יעקב's strong position.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not save רב הונא's first point. He still loses on the middle of the roof (step 13). Only the second attack is pushed off.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא tool: a source sometimes picks the extreme case to show the full strength of one opinion. That does not mean the easier case is agreed upon.

phrases.english: רב הונא can say to you:
they argue about the middle of the roof,
and the same is true on the edge of the roof.
And the reason they argue about the middle of the roof
is to show you the strength of רבי יעקב's view,
that even in the middle of the roof he also rules it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second attack in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the source chose the case it did (to show the strength of רבי יעקב's view).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא set the argument in the middle, the edge must be agreed to be kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument covers both the middle and the edge. The middle was chosen to show רבי יעקב allows even that case.

steps.title: רבי יעקב's Test for Corner Posts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that if four posts are stuck in the ground with סכך on top, רבי יעקב checks whether each post is thick enough to be carved into an L-shape with a טפח on each side. If so, it counts as a דיומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone stuck four posts in the ground and put סכך on top, רבי יעקב says: we picture each post being carved and split into an L-shape. If it would have a טפח in this direction and a טפח in that direction, it counts as a double post (דיומד). If not, it does not count as a double post.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about the same case of four posts stuck in the ground. This one explains how רבי יעקב measures the posts so that they count as walls by themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דיומד is a corner post shaped like an L, so it covers a little of two walls at once. רבי יעקב says a thick round or square post qualifies if you could carve an L out of it with a טפח on each side. If the post is too thin for that, it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A double post: an L-shaped corner piece that counts as part of two walls
Grooved and split: carved so an L-shape is left

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody actually carves the posts. רבי יעקב only asks us to picture it, to see if the post is thick enough.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If one stuck four posts into the ground
and placed the roof covering on top of them,
Rabbi Yaakov says: we look at it
any post that, if it were grooved and split,
phrases.notes: Picture cutting a notch out of the post so what is left looks like the letter L.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶן טֶפַח לְכָאן וְטֶפַח לְכָאן
phrases.english: would have a handbreadth this way and a handbreadth that way
are judged as a double post,
and if not,
they are not judged as a double post.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נָעַץ אַרְבָּעָה קוּנְדֵּיסִין בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same four-posts case that explains רבי יעקב's reasoning: the posts count as corner walls (דיומד) by themselves, without needing house walls below.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יעקב, a post counts as a דיומד if it could be carved into an L-shape with a טפח on each side.

steps.title: רבי יעקב and חכמים Disagree on How Small Walls Can Be
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the reason: רבי יעקב holds that the corner pieces of a סוכה need only be a טפח. חכמים require two full walls and a third wall of at least a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יעקב used to say: the double posts of a סוכה need only be a טפח. But חכמים say: the סוכה is not kosher unless it has two proper walls, and a third that can be even just a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the background of רבי יעקב's ruling and gives the opposing view of חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יעקב, four L-shaped corners of a טפח each are enough walls for a סוכה. חכמים say this is not enough: you need two complete walls, and only the third wall may be as small as a טפח. So in the four-posts case, רבי יעקב says kosher and חכמים say not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Two walls in their proper, complete form
A third wall that can be even one handbreadth
Only when there are; not kosher until

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב: four corner posts of a טפח each make a kosher סוכה. חכמים: two full walls plus a third of at least a טפח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the four-posts dispute that רב הונא and רב נחמן were discussing: whether small corner pieces alone can count as the walls of a סוכה.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yaakov used to say:
the double posts of a sukkah are a handbreadth,
and the Sages say:
it is not kosher until there are two walls in their proper form,
and a third, even a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יעקב's ruling in step 16 and the opposing view of חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יעקב: corner pieces of a טפח are enough. חכמים: two full walls and a third of at least a טפח.

steps.title: Where Do We Learn the Ten-טפחים Minimum?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: a סוכה lower than ten טפחים is not kosher. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And one that is not ten טפחים high" is not kosher. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule about the minimum height of a סוכה and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about a סוכה that is too tall or about its walls. Now the גמרא turns to the minimum height. It wants a source for the number ten.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
High, tall
Ten handbreadths, the minimum height of a סוכה

phrases.english: "And one that is not ten handbreadths high."
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from our משנה, which says such a סוכה is not kosher.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יעקב discussion and starts a new section of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים high.

steps.title: The Sages Who Teach the Source, and a Note on One Name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names four sages who taught the source for the ten-טפחים rule. Then, as a side note, it says that throughout סדר מועד some swap רבי יוחנן for רבי יונתן in this pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב, רבי חנינא, רבי יוחנן and רב חביבא taught the source. A side note: in all of סדר מועד, wherever this pair appears, some take out רבי יוחנן and put in רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It names the sages who teach the source, but the teaching itself comes next. First it adds a side note about one of the names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names come in two pairs: רב and רבי חנינא, then רבי יוחנן and רב חביבא. The side note says that in the second pair, some versions say רבי יונתן instead of רבי יוחנן, and this happens all through סדר מועד. This does not change the law. It only fixes who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the משנה that covers שבת and the holidays
A pair of sages
They replace or swap out
They bring in or insert

steps.confusionAlert: The actual source for ten טפחים is not given yet. This step only names who will teach it. The teaching comes next.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav and Rabbi Chanina
and Rabbi Yochanan and Rav Chaviva taught.
Throughout all of the order of Moed,
wherever this pair appears,
phrases.notes: He means the second pair: רבי יוחנן and רב חביבא.

phrases.english: they swap out Rabbi Yochanan
and put in Rabbi Yonatan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַב חֲבִיבָא מַתְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 18 by naming who teaches the source, and adds a side note about one name.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Introduces the sages who teach the source. The source itself comes next.

steps.title: The Ark and its cover add up to ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The source for the ten-טפחים rule starts here. The ארון was nine טפחים tall and the כפורת was one טפח, ten in total. The פסוק says ה׳ spoke from above the כפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ארון was nine טפחים tall, and the כפורת was one טפח thick. So here we have ten. And it is written: "I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the כפורת."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins laying out the source for why a סוכה needs ten טפחים by adding up the height of the ארון and the כפורת. This is the setup piece; the proof is not finished yet and continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine טפחים for the ארון plus one טפח for the כפורת gives exactly ten. The פסוק places ה׳'s speaking "above the כפורת," so the number ten becomes tied to the place where the Divine Presence met משה. The גמרא has not yet said how this connects to סוכה. It is only putting the pieces in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ark of the Covenant in the משכן, which held the לוחות
The gold cover that sat on top of the ארון
A handbreadth, a basic unit of measurement
"So here there are ten": adding up the two heights

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the proof is complete here. So far the גמרא has only shown that the ארון plus the כפורת equals ten and that ה׳ spoke from above it. The link to the minimum height of a סוכה comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first half of the source for the משנה's rule that a סוכה under ten טפחים is not kosher.

phrases.english: The Ark was nine [handbreadths tall],
phrases.notes: The תורה says the ארון was one and a half אמות tall. With an אמה of six טפחים, that comes to nine.

phrases.english: and the Ark cover was one handbreadth [thick].
So here there are ten.
And it is written: "I will meet with you there
and I will speak with you from above the Ark cover"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָרוֹן תִּשְׁעָה, וְכַפּוֹרֶת טֶפַח — הֲרֵי כָּאן עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 19 named the sages who taught the source. This step begins giving the actual content of that source.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a סוכה lower than ten טפחים is not kosher
steps.raayaSupportSource: The combined height of the ארון (nine טפחים) and the כפורת (one טפח), together with the פסוק in שמות 25:22 that ה׳ spoke from above the כפורת
